REPORT OF THE CHAIRMAN 


AND DIRECTOR GENERAL 


n 1986-1987 the Montreal YMCA celebrated the 
135th anniversary of its founding and continued 
its essential role in the Montreal community 

of developing innovative projects and programs 
which respond to present-day needs. Our fiscal year ending 

May 31, 1987 was extremely positive and reflective of our guiding 
principle of self-funding and investing in the future development 
of the Montreal milieu. 


The past year was one of great accomplishments, well-met 
challenges and exciting plans for the future. Our YMCA is set 
to meet the challenge of the 21st century. 


More than 300 people attended our 135th anniversary banquet, 
held on November 25, 1986. Two guest speakers — Gerry Weiner, 
Canada’s Minister of State for Immigration, and Philippe de Gaspé 
Beaubien, Chairman and C.E.0. of Télémédia Corporation — 
praised the YMCA’s record of involvement and outlined the vital 
role non-profit organizations can play within their communities. 
Among those in attendance and duly recognized were a number 
of former chairmen of the Metropolitan Board of Directors, the 
living authors of a good part of the Association’s 135 years of 
history. 


Montrealers at large had an opportunity to relive our Association’s 
past, thanks to an eight-week photographic exhibition held at the 
Archives nationales du Québec, in Old Montreal. The exhibition 
was made possible by the generous support of the Ministére des 
Affaires culturelles — Archives nationales du Québec and 

La Presse. 


Sol Kasimer, Director General; Bernard W. Matte, Chairman of 
the Metropolitain Board. 


Past accomplishments have provided us with a solid base for 
present dynamism and future growth. 


A YMCA 
AT COMPLEXE 
GU Y-FAVREAU 


ta gathering of several hun- 
dred community and cor- 
porate leaders, the ninth 
Montreal-area branch was 
opened at Complexe Guy-Favreau. Over 
1,300 new members are now part of the 
YMCA family, taking part in a wide range of 
programs and services designed for both the 
working population in the Complexe and 
the surrounding community-at-large. 


A YOUTH ENTERPRISE 
CENTRE IN MONTREAL 


he Youth Enterprise Centre also 

opened its doors in 1987. The 

Montreal Y.E.C. program was created 

to address the ever-growing prob- 
lem of youth unemployment. It is aimed 
mainly at young people under 30 years of 
age who wish to start a business. The pro- 
gram offers an introduction to business 
techniques and helps turn ideas into con- 
crete projects. The Y.E.C. is located on Prince 
Street, in Montreal. Over 20 young en- 
trepreneurs have already launched their 
own companies! The Montreal Youth Enter- 
prise Centre is part of a national project into 
which the federal government has injected 
over $10,000,000 for youth job-creation. 
The YMCA submitted the initial proposal for 
the project, which, in addition to govern- 
ment support, has also received backing 
from the private sector (in particular, IBM 
Canada, which has graciously supplied 
equipment for the ten Y.E.C.s across the 
country). Al Hatton ensures the overall su- 
pervision of the pan-Canadian Y.E.C. pro- 
gram from his office in Montreal. Dian 
Cohen is the head of the national advisory 
committee, and John McBain is the chair- 
man of the Montreal Y.E.C. advisory 
committee. 


A PRIZE 
OF EXCELLENCE 


he Montreal business community 

has publicly recognized the excep- 

tional success and excellence 

of our Job Generation program, 
which is intended for unemployed young 
people 18 to 30 years of age who are look- 
ing for work. Job Generation was recently 


awarded an “‘Iris” trophy for its work in 
this field by the Association of Human 
Resource Professionals of the Province 

of Quebec. The special Iris award presented 
to the YMCA underlines the energy and 
professionalism of the program’s team of 
employees and volunteers, who are led by 
Job Generation Director Graham Weeks. 


TWO LOCAL CAPITAL 
CAMPAIGNS 


he Montreal community has gener- 

ously supported YMCA projects for 

more than 135 years. Since 1985, 

the Association has been appealing 
to our fellow citizens’ community spirit 
through its five-year Capital Development 
Campaign because certain YMCA buildings 
date back to 1912, while others cannot meet 
the needs of the areas they serve. We have 
already renovated the arena run by the 
Hochelaga-Maisonneuve branch, and the 
Centre-ville, International, Notre-Dame- 
de-Grace and Saint-Laurent branches have 
been modernized to comply with present-day 
standards. 


As for the West Island and Westmount 
branches, major construction and renova- 
tion work is required. This is why the West 
Island YMCA has unveiled plans for a 
completely new building and, under the 
chairmanship of Les McAuley, has launched 
a local capital campaign aimed at raising 
$610,000. This sum will go towards building 
new facilities and transforming existing pro- 
gram space. The total cost of the project will 
be $5,700,000. Over 500 West Island volun- 
teers are hard at work raising funds for the 
local campaign. They are assisted by the 
Montreal YMCA Foundation, which is led 

by Director General Jean Robert Nolet. The 
new West Island YMCA will be a complete, 
family-oriented centre, where young and old 
will grow together. 


As for the Westmount YMCA, workers will 
begin renovating and expanding the 
branch's 75-year-old building in 1987-1988. 
Under the chairmanship of Richard L. Cooper, 
a $3,000,000 capital campaign was 
launched a few months ago within the 
Westmount community. Once again, local 
residents are enthusiastically supporting our 
mission and social role. Hundreds of volun- 
teers are contributing wholeheartedly to 

the campaign, organizing the fund-raising 
efforts, recruiting new members and 
soliciting funds from the community. The 
YMCA tradition carries on in Westmount. 


ithin the walls of its safely- 
designed, comfortable 
buildings, the YMCA offers 
a wide array of programs 
designed to help the Association fulfil its 
mission, which focusses on the harmonious 
development of the individual in spirit, mind 
and body. In 1987 we concentrated on 
lifestyle programs, now offered by all of 
our branches, which zero is on health 
and self-help measures. Last year, over 
115,000 people benefitted directly from 
YMCA programs and services. 


400,000 
MONTREALERS 
PARTICIPATE 

IN THE CHALLENGE 


ontrealers have amply 

proven their commitment 

to fitness: the memorable 

CrownLife-PARTICIPaction 
Challenge, organized in our city by the 
YMCA, aroused considerable interest. 
Following a challenge extended by Mayor 
Jean Doré to his Toronto counterpart, nearly 
400,000 Montrealers phoned the Challenge 
headquarters, located at Complexe 
Desjardins, to confirm that they had partici- 
pated in 15 minutes of physical activity 
on the day of the event. Montreal was the 
proud victor, and the YMCA, thanks to the 
help of a large number of volunteers, coor- 
dinated by Conrad Sauvé, Director, Inter- 
national YMCA, upheld its reputation as an 
efficient community organizer. With the 
solid support of the entire Montreal commu- 
nity, the CrownLife-PARTICIPaction-Y MCA- 
Montreal partnership was truly a winning 
team.

MESSAGE FROM THE CHAIRMAN 


OF THE MONTREAL YMCA FOUNDATION 


The Montreal YMCA Foundation was created 

in 1983. Its objectives are as follows: 

¢ “To solicit, by all appropriate means, and 
receive all donations, contributions, 
bequests and subscriptions of a charitable 
nature, in kind or in cash, for the exclu- 
sive advantage and use of the Young Men's 
Christian Association of Montreal; 

© “To these ends, to acquire, retain, 
administer, invest and reinvest these 
donations, contributions, bequests, and 
subscriptions free of charge, and channel 
these funds, with the exception of those 
needed to cover the administrative costs 
of the Corporation, exclusively to the 
Young Men’s Christian Association of 
Montreal.” 

(Foundation statement of mission) 


For the past two years the Foundation has 
been led by a 30-member Board of Directors, 
whose members represent three different 
sectors: corporations and foundations that 
have donated to the YMCA, volunteer 
fund-raisers and the Montreal YMCA. The 
Board members’ names are as follows: 
Jacques Baylaucq 

(Mrs.) Jean Bernard 

Jonathan Birks 

Bruce Bishop 

Roland Breton 

Marcel Coté 

John Churchill-Smith 

John E. Cleghorn 

Richard L. Cooper 

Victor M. Drury 

John Economides 

L. Yves Fortier 

Derek Hannaford 

Albert Hudon 

Solomon Kasimer 

Raymond Leduc 

Claude Lemay 

Len Liben 

Maurice A. Massé 

Bernard W. Matte 

Les McAuley 

Louis Paul Nolet 

Frank Peterson 

Philip O’Brien 

Pierre Riverin 

Glenn R. Rourke 

Pierre Shooner 

J. Robert Swidler 

Robert S. Vineberg 


In order to ensure the sound management 
of the Corporation, the Board of Directors 
set up four bodies: the Finance, Investment, 
Needs Analysis and Nominating Committees. 


The Finance Committee looks after the 
Corporation’s operating budget, monitors 
the various fund-raising campaigns and 
draws up financial statements. It is chaired 
by the Corporation treasurer, Bruce Bishop, 
who is assisted by Bernard Dubé, Len Liben 
and Roland Breton. 


The members of the Investment Committee 
— Derek Hannaford, John Economides, 
William Ridley and Maurice A. Massé (the 
latter serving as chairman) — are responsi- 
ble for investing funds from two sources: 
money raised by the various campaigns, 
and money donated to the Corporation's 
Endowment and Bequest program. 


The third body, the Needs Analysis 
Committee, examines requests for financial 
assistance submitted by the Montreal YMCA. 
It is made up of four members: Frank 
Peterson, Pierre Riverin, Glenn R. Rourke 
and Victor M. Drury (Committee chairman). 
Following a preliminary analysis by the 
Corporation staff, requests for financial 
assistance are forwarded to the Committee 
for further study. The Committee members 
subsequently submit their recommendations 
to the Board of Directors for acceptance 

or refusal. 


The fourth committee created by the Board 
of Directors is chaired by J. Robert Swidler, 
who is backed up by Jacques Baylaucq, 
Marcel Coté and Solomon Kasimer. In 
keeping with the Foundation by-laws, the 
Nominating Committee submits recommen- 
dations as to the make-up of the Board of 
Directors and the Executive Committee, and 
identifies suitable candidates for Foundation 
governors and honorary members. 


The first group of governors and honorary 
members will be elected at the Foundation’s 
annual meeting scheduled for October 5, 
1987. The candidates are all men and 
women who have contributed significantly 
to the success of the Corporation’s five-year 
Capital Development Campaign. Their names 
are as follows: 

G. Drummond Birks

Model of the new building for the West Island YMCA 


A second group of worthy individuals, 
consisting of former Corporation directors 
who have served the Foundation since its 
creation, will also be honoured: 

L. Yves Fortier 

Les McAuley 

Len Liben 

Roy D. Locke 

Louis Paul Nolet 

Frank Peterson 

Bruce Bishop 

Harvey Thomson 


The Montreal YMCA Capital Development 
Campaign, which was set in motion in April 
1985, has made considerable progress over 
the past 12 months. Close to $3,000,000 
was donated or pledged to the Campaign 
between June 1, 1986, and May 31, 1987. 
The Campaign has already raised a total of 
$8,000,000, or 62 % of its five-year, 
$13,000,000 objective. I wish to underline 
in particular the impressive work of the 


co-chairmen of the Corporations and Founda- ° 


tions Campaign, John Churchill-Smith and 
Ghislain Hawey, and the chairmen of the 
West Island and Westmount fund-raising 
drives, Les McAuley and Richard L. Cooper. 


Thanks to the generosity of the private sec- 
tor, the Foundation Board of Directors was 
able to donate $755,000 to the Montreal 
YMCA over 1986-1987 fiscal year. These 
funds were used for preliminary work at the 
new West Island building, repairs within 


the existing network of facilities and replace- 


ment of outdated equipment at all YMCA 
branches. 


In closing, I wish to thank the 1,000-odd 
volunteers who have contributed their time 
and energy to the various Foundation fund- 
raising programs. Without their zeal and 
devotion, we would not have been able to 
raise more than 62% of our overall Capital 
Development Campaign objective in so short 
a time, nor would we have been able to 
solicit fully $600,000 for the Endowment 
and Bequest program. 


Philip O’Brien 


REPORT OF THE DIRECTOR GENERAL 


OF THE MONTREAL YMCA FOUNDATION 


I am pleased to provide you with the follow- 
ing update on the progress made over the 
past 12 months by the Montreal YMCA 
Foundation fund-raising programs. The 
Sustaining Membership program has been 
in existence for three years, and the Endow- 
ment and Bequest and Corporations and 
Foundations programs have now been under 
way for two full years. 


SUSTAINING MEMBERSHIP 
PROGRAM 

Since its creation three years ago, the 
Sustaining Membership program has raised 
a total of $317,683. The Foundation has 
transferred all potential corporate and foun- 
dation donors from the program prospect 
list to that of the Corporations and Founda- 
tions Campaign (which is also part of the 
overall Capital Development Campaign). 


The Chairman of the Sustaining Member- 
ship program, Mr. Claude Lemay, joins with 
the honorary chairpersons in thanking cam- 
paign donors for their generosity. Thanks 

to them, the program’s third year has been 

a resounding success. The Foundation also 
wishes to express its deeply-felt gratitude for 
the contributions in time and energy of the 
hundreds of campaign volunteers particular- 
ly those who have helped the West Island, 
Pointe-Saint-Charles, Hochelaga-Maisonneuve 
and Westmount YMCAs and the Hudson 
Program Centre reach their respective fund- 
raising goals. The overall 1984-1991 objec- 
tive for the Sustaining Membership program 
has been set at $1,370,000. The program is 
aimed at past and present YMCA committee 
members and employees, YMCA Members 
and program participants, and friends of the 
Association. 


ENDOWMENT AND BEQUEST 
PROGRAM 

Under the dynamic leadership of Chair- 
man Maurice A. Massé, the Endowment 
and Bequest Committee members (Kalman 
Samuels, Keith Farquharson, William Ridley, 
Harvey Corn, Michael Gutwillig, Roy D. 
Locke, Alex Duff, Marcel Adams and Frank 
Peterson) solicit donations from long- 
standing friends of the Montreal YMCA. The 
Committee's goal is to endow the Associa- 
tion, which was founded in 1851, with a 
solid financial base for future growth. 


In planning their estates, donors may sti- 
pulate that their bequests be allocated to a 
specific branch or program, or go toward 

a given area of involvement (camperships, 
youth programs, leadership training, new 
facilities, land purchases, etc.). No matter 
what their amount, commemorative dona- 
tions to the Montreal YMCA Endowment 
Fund are always greatly appreciated. To date, 
the Endowment and Bequest program has 
received immediate donations totalling 
$77,373, bequests of $509,435, confirmed 
bequest pledges in the order of $347,000 
and fifteen confirmed pledges of unspecified 
amounts. As shown by the above figures, 
the program progressed significantly over 
the 1986-1987 fiscal year. 


Last year, for the fourth year running, the 
Montreal YMCA Heritage Club members met 
at the Mount Stephen Club to underline 
their interest in the Association. The Club is 
made up of more than 40 men and women 
who firmly believe in the mission and tradi- 
tional values of the YMCA, and wish to 
ensure that the Association’s heritage is 
passed on to future generations. 


Each Club member has made provisions for 
the YMCA in planning his or her estate by 
promising to make a cash donation, naming 
the YMCA as an insurance-policy beneficiary 
or contributing to the Association during 
his or her lifetime. 


CORPORATIONS AND 
FOUNDATIONS PROGRAM 

I wish to underline the extraordinary efforts 
of the following people, who worked hard 
under Co-Chairmen John Churchill-Smith 
and Ghislain Hawey: 


(Mrs.) Jean Bernard, Philip O’Brien, Louis 
Paul Nolet, Walter Light, Thomas Galt, John 
E. Cleghorn, Grant C. Reuber, John Rogers, 
Doug.McDougall, Victor M. Drury, Bernard 
W. Matte, Lynn Goth, Bruce Bishop, William 
I.M. Turner Jr., G. Drummond Birks, Logan 
Brown, Denton Clark, David Braide, A. Jean 
De Grandpré, Raymond V. Cyr, Gérard 
Limoges, Roger A. Beauchemin, Roland 
Breton, Marcel Coté, L. Yves Fortier, Brian 
Gallory and Robert S. Vineberg. 


At the end of the second full year of the 
Montreal YMCA Capital Development Cam- 
paign, the results of the three main divi- 
sions of the Corporations and Foundations 
program are as follows: 


(1) Lead Gifts division: 
Twenty-four of the 27 target corporations 
and foundations have so far agreed to 
contribute, and the others will notify us 
as to their decision in 1987-1988. 


Total contributions: $3,579,000 (ie., 
98% of our target of $3,700,000). 


(2) Major Gifts division: 
Ninety-one of the 156 target corporations 
and foundations have so far agreed to 
contribute, and the others will notify us 
as to their decision in 1987-1988. 


Total contributions: $1,370,147 (ie., 
68.5% of our target of $2,000,000). 


(3) Thousand Plus division: 
One hundred and twenty-nine of the 
458 target corporations and foundations 
have so far agreed to contribute, and the 
others will notify us as to their decision 
in 1987-1988. 
Total contributions: $300,025 (i.e, 15 % 
of our target of $2,000,000). 


In brief, the Corporations and Foundations 
program, which is part of the broader Capi- 
tal Development Campaign, has already 
raised 68 % of its overall goal of $7,700,000. 
Once again, I heartily congratulate all of 

our canvassers, and sincerely thank them for 
their invaluable assistance. To all of the 
corporations and foundations that have 
chosen to support the Montreal YMCA, 

I extend my warmest gratitude. 


WEST ISLAND YMCA CAPITAL 
CAMPAIGN 

After only ten months of canvassing, the 
West Island YMCA Capital Campaign chair- 
man, Les McAuley, reported that more than 
$400,000 had been raised within the local 
community. This amount represents close to 
75% of the Campaign target of $550,000. 


The Campaign has been split into five divi- 
sions, all of which have produced strong 
results. (The following figures were com- 
piled as at May 31st 1987.) 


I. YMCA Resources division: 
Objective: $35,000 
Raised so far: $25,905 (74% ) 


This division is composed of Board mem- 
bers, staff and participants in YMCA pro- 
grams. The branch Board of Management 
has demonstrated outstanding leadership by 
raising $8,885 in personal gifts from 

19 Board members. 


West Island employees have shown equal 
commitment: full-time personnel and close 
to 50 part-time instructors have donated 

a total of $2,089. 


Finally, nearly 400 program participants 
contributed close to $15,000 to the Capital 
Campaign in 1986 alone. Eighty-two of 
these donors also worked as volunteer 
canvassers, 


The YMCA Resources division is led by Peter 
Rollit (Board), Scott Haldane (staff) and 
Eleanor O'Neill (participants). 


Il. Special Names division: 
Objective: $150,000 
Raised so far: $131,194 (87 % ) 


Over 70 canvassers have received donations 
from 193 West Island residents. This divi- 
sion is chaired by Victoria Stewart. 


Ill. Business and Industry division: 
Objective: $150,000 
Raised so far: $116,997 (78%) 


Nearly 100 canvassers have received dona- 
tions from 259 West Island companies. 

A very successful raffle organized by West 
Island banks (coordinated by John Fougere 
of the Royal Bank) raised $18,000. The 
division is chaired by Murray Heselton 

of Metropolitan Stores. 


From left to right: Bernard W. Matte, Chairman of the Montreal YMCA 
Board of Directors; Richard French, MNA for Westmount and Quebec 
Minister of Communications; Richard L, Cooper, chairman of the 
fund-raising campaign; Brian Gallery, mayor of Westmount; Donald 
Johnston, federal MP for Saint-Henri-Westmount; Doug McDougall, 
chairman of the Westmount YMCA; Victor M. Drury, former chairman 
of the Montreal YMCA Board of Directors; Hope Korytko, Westmount 
YMCA executive director; Albert Hudon, chairman of the Building 
Committee; Sol Kasimer, Montreal YMCA Director General. 


Sketch of the renovated building of the Westmount YMCA 


IV. Municipal Government division: 
Objective: $250,000 
Raised so far: $101,498 (41% ) 


Nine ouf of twelve West Island municipali- 
ties (Baie-D'Urfé, Beaconsfield, Dollard- 
des-Ormeaux, fle-Bizard, Pointe-Claire, 
Pierrefonds, Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue, 
Sainte-Geneviéve and Senneville) have so far 
contributed to the Campaign. We will be 
returning to four of these municipalities 

in the fall, as well as seeking initial com- 
mitments from the remaining three. 


V. Special Events division: 
Objective: $25,000 
Raised so far: $26,293 (105 % ) 


This was the first division to reach its objec- 
tive. Two extremely successful events, held 
under the direction of Rachel Bacher (Aero- 
bathon) and Norman Macleod (Golf Tour- 
nament), both surpassed their goals. Both of 
these events will be repeated in 1988. 


More than 300 volunteers have worked on 
the Campaign to date. A further 200 volun- 
teers will hopefully raise another $18,500 
from YMCA Resources, $45,000 from Special 
Names, $25,000 from Businesses and Indus- 
tries, $61,500 from Municipal Governments 
and $70,000 from Special Events. The 
Campaign will continue until the new West 
Island YMCA facility opens in June 1988. 


WESTMOUNT YMCA CAPITAL 
CAMPAIGN 

The Westmount YMCA's $3,000,000 Capital 
Campaign (a branch of the Montreal YMCA’s 
$13,000,000 Capital Development Campaign) 
was Officially launched at Victoria Hall on 
February 23, 1987. Hailed as one of the 
largest face-to-face fund-raising drives ever 
undertaken in Canada, it is a truly 
community-based effort. Led by Chairman 
Richard L. Cooper, more than 800 volun- 
teers are involved in various aspects of this 
massive fund-raising effort. These volun- 
teers are the lifeblood of the operation: their 
support and contributions will ensure the 
ongoing existence of the YMCA as a tradi- 
tional part of the Westmount community. 


The Westmount Campaign is divided 

into six sub-sectors: Special Names (goal: 
$2,350,000), Governments (goal: $400,000), 
YMCA Resources (goal: $75,000), Small Busi- 
nesses and Professionals (goal: $75,000), 
Special Events (goal: $50,000) and Residen- 
tial and Direct Mail (goal: $50,000). 


In May 1987 a first special event was held 
— the ‘Prelude Ball,’ at the Westmount 
Arena. Over 800 guests attended this black-tie 
evening, which raised a total of $70,000. 
Chaired by Judith Webster, the event was a 
huge success both in terms of money raised 
and of community support and participation. 


The YMCA Resource division kicked off its 
fund-raising efforts in February 1987, under 
the co-chairmanship of Doug McDougall and 
Hope Korytko. Thanks to the solid support 
of the Westmount YMCA Board members 
and staff, fully 71% of the target had been 
attained by the end of the fiscal year. 


The Small Business and Professionals 
division was launched in April 1987. Led by 
Co-Chairpersons George Alevisatos and Ruth 
Shine, 100 canvassers are currently solicit- 
ing support from 550 local small businesses 
and professionals. 


The Special Names sector is well under way. 
Under the leadership of Richard L. Cooper, 
Nathan Scott, Michael Huband, Brian Aune, 
Diana Colby and Derek Hannaford, canvass- 
ers will be approaching more than 3,000 
potential donors on a one-to-one basis. 


Victory Drury, chairman of the Govern- 
ments division, has been working with the 
Montreal YMCA and community leaders to 
secure support for the Campaign from the 
various levels of government. 


As of May 31, 1987, $600,000 (i.e., 20%) of 
the overall Campaign objective has been 
raised. The funds will be used to renovate 
and expand the 75-year-old Westmount 
facility, which will be transformed into a 
35,000-square-foot family YMCA. The new 
facility will be a place to bring people to- 
gether, help participants grow, encourage 
responsible leadership, respect the rights of 
others, build self-reliance and integrity, and 
strive for excellence in all areas of personal 
development. 


Jean Robert Nolet

he Montreal YMCA Capital Development Campaign, the fifth major fund-raising effort undertaken by the Association since the start 

of the century, got under way in 1985. As in the case of the earlier drives, the Campaign has received a significant level of support from 

the Montreal business community. 
Fund-raising will be spread out over five years, from 1985 to 1990. Messrs. John Churchill-Smith and Ghislain Hawey, the hard-working 
co-chairmen of the Campaign, join with the honorary chairpersons and the hundreds of volunteer canvassers in thanking the following
